standout_why: Compared against cartechtalk.com, gearjury.com, wikidashcam.org and our own dealectric.com/best-4-channel-dash-cam, all opened 2026-11-21. Cartechtalk already says a hardwire kit is included with the G980H 4-channel set it lists, and our page says the opposite, so rivals hold part of this. None names the kit model, its connector, its price or a card-size limit; cartechtalk says outright that the G980H's maximum card capacity is not stated. Gearjury does not cover the G980H at all, and wikidashcam lists the Vantrue E360 with no hardwire or accessory detail. The two cited pages could not be compared: Tom's Guide returned only navigation text and Car and Driver blocked the fetch. The score is 1 because the gap is real but no maker document was opened to fill it; with the kit model, price and in-box status from botslab.com it would be a 3.
decides: It does not change the pick yet. ChatGPT made its Botslab G980H choice conditional on the parking-mode hardware fitting inside $250, and that condition is still open. The G980H's link price leaves room under $250 for a kit, but the kit's price is unread. Before publishing, one read of the botslab.com 4-camera listing and its Type-C hardwire kit page must settle whether the kit is in the box, because cartechtalk and our own page contradict each other. The Vantrue E360 and E360 ACE are in budget at a partner store and are the only candidates that answer the 'actual 360° panoramic' reading of the question, but their kit and accessory pairings are also unread.
